correctness.rationale: For x_i=f(a_i) and y_i=f(b_i), the equations are x_i+sum_(j>=i)y_j=0 and y_i+sum_(j<=i)x_j=0. Their consecutive differences force (x_(i+1),y_(i+1))=(x_i+y_i,-x_i), and the two endpoint equations are x_1+y_1=x_n+y_n=0. Conversely the consecutive differences and endpoints recover every original equation, including n=1. The transfer matrix has cube -I and sixth power I. From (t,-t) the six states are (t,-t),(0,-t),(-t,0),(-t,t),(0,t),(t,0); the last endpoint is satisfied for t nonzero precisely when n=1 mod 3. Restricting x_1 to the allowed labels gives t in {-1,0,1}, and every entry in the orbit is then allowed. The successive weight terms 0,-t,-t,0,t,t cancel per period and leave zero at n=1 mod 6 and -2t at n=4 mod 6. This proves the full classification and maximum. Independent direct closed-neighborhood enumeration of 597870 ternary assignments for n=1 through 6 gives the same full solution sets and weights; exact rational rank checks through n=20 give the predicted real nullity 0 or 1.
residual_risks: The independent finite checks are corroboration. The transfer calculation proves the result for all n and does not cover arbitrary Ferrers shapes with repeated neighborhoods.

value.rationale: The half graph is a natural canonical chain graph for the established balanced-domination invariant. The result goes beyond detecting a nonzero kernel: it identifies every feasible labeling and shows why two real-kernel-positive residues give different optimal weights. The exact phase and complete family are useful for distinguishing balanced domination from mere adjacency singularity at -1.
residual_risks: No extension to arbitrary chain graphs or other domination definitions is claimed.
